newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euro stocks face sharp falls after U.S. dive.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euro stocks face sharp falls after U.S. dive.

text.p: European stock markets faced a day of heavy losses on Monday after Wall Street suffered its second biggest points loss in history on Friday.
A weak dollar and worries about U.S. profits wiped 247.37 points, or more than three percent, off the Dow Jones Industrial Average to 7,694.66 on Friday.
Wall Street's falls prompted heavy selling in Asian markets on Monday, many of which are also being undermined by currency turmoil in the region.
Continental European markets, many of which were closed on Friday for a holiday, are likely to be hit more than London which has already reacted to the early stages of the Dow plunge.

German shares fell heavily in pre-bourse electronic trading on Monday. The IBIS DAX index fell as low as 3,965.31, down 2.75 percent or 112,28 points from Friday's close of electronic trade, before paring losses to 3,976.36.

In London, the FTSE 100 index opened 1.48 percent lower at 4,794.0 on Monday, hammered by Wall Street's sell-off and follow through selling to the UK market's biggest one-day point loss since the October 1987 crash.
Thee FTSE 100 had already shed 2.5 percent on Friday, its largest percent loss in five years.
The initial sell-off may be met with some caution, however, since the U.S. bond market did not fall on Friday and investors were given the weekend to assess the market's condition.

"I think what will happen is that the market-makers will mark it down quickly, and then there will be a pause for the investor reaction and that will determine the next move," said Richard Jeffrey, head of research at Charterhouse Tilney.
He said the London market would also be waiting for direction from Wall Street, but fears that British interest rates may have to rise again during the rest of the year would weigh on shares.
Some traders said the FTSE 100 could drop even further as it catches up with the Dow drop, which reverberated to the Asian markets. The 225-share Nikkei average in Tokyo fell 1.47 percent.
"I would think it would have to fall at least 80 points...and it could easily be down 100 points," one London trader said.

"The only salvation is that the U.S. long bond held up...and there was no great selling on Friday," he added. "We are really going to have to get some clarification and wait for New York to see if we get any type of rally."
The dollar remained under pressure against the mark on jitters about German interest rates before the Bundesbank holds its first meeting on Thursday following the summer break.
Markets are also awaiting the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee -- the central bank's policy-making arm -- which meets to consider interest rates on Tuesday.
The dollar remained soft due to the German rate jitters but stayed above 1.81 marks after hitting an 1.8060 overnight low.
